inspiration.observed_pattern: A scalar query combines DATE_ADD with day, year, and HOUR_MINUTE intervals, then uses EXTRACT to project calendar components from timestamp expressions.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Rewritten as an independently authored maintenance schedule report. NOW() is replaced with fixed DATETIME column values; DATE_ADD computes due, renewal, and preparation timestamps, including a negative HOUR_MINUTE interval, while EXTRACT returns year, month, day, and hour parts. The source schema, names, and values are not copied.

fixture_notes: Job 101 starts on January 31 to exercise MariaDB's end-of-month month-add behavior; job 102 starts on February 15. The negative HOUR_MINUTE interval subtracts 90 minutes, and all calendar parts come from fixed DATETIME values.
determinism_notes: All timestamps and job IDs are fixed; the output is ordered by the unique job ID. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE maintenance_jobs (job_id INT PRIMARY KEY, asset VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, scheduled_at DATETIME NOT NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT job_id, asset, scheduled_at, DATE_ADD(scheduled_at, INTERVAL 2 DAY) AS due_at, DATE_ADD(scheduled_at, INTERVAL 1 MONTH) AS renewal_at, DATE_ADD(scheduled_at, INTERVAL '-1:30' HOUR_MINUTE) AS prep_at, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM scheduled_at) AS scheduled_year, EXTRACT(MONTH FROM scheduled_at) AS scheduled_month, EXTRACT(DAY FROM scheduled_at) AS scheduled_day, EXTRACT(HOUR FROM scheduled_at) AS scheduled_hour FROM maintenance_jobs ORDER BY job_id
